name: md-planner
description: Plan projects in Markdown: milestones, tasks, Gantt, Kanban, team capacity, test plans, AI estimates, MCP agents and manager-ready exports.
author: ACRO

viewsWelcome.contents:
No plan in this workspace (no project.md in the plan folder).
[New project](command:planner.newProject)
Or let an AI agent build the whole plan from a description: connect it to the planner's MCP server, then ask it to plan your project.
[Configure MCP for Claude Code](command:planner.configureMcp)
[Add the md-planner skill for AI agents](command:planner.addAgentSkill)
A plan is a folder of Markdown files (`plan/` by default, setting `planner.planFolder`).
[Open the user manual](command:planner.openManual)

There are no milestones yet. A milestone is a phase or deliverable with a target date; its tasks are scheduled automatically.
[Add milestone](command:planner.addMilestone)

There is nobody in the team yet. People get tasks (owner), a capacity and time off, which the schedule respects.
[Add person](command:planner.addPerson)

The inbox is empty. Capture ideas, requests and reminders here, and plan them into a milestone later.
[Capture to inbox](command:planner.captureInbox)

No punch items. Punch items are defects and open points, usually raised from failed test steps.
[Add punch item](command:planner.addPunchItem)

No test plans yet. A test plan is a Markdown file in the plan's tests/ folder with test cases and steps.
[Read how in the user manual](command:planner.openManual)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Markdown Project Planner
walkthroughs.description: Plan projects in Markdown files: schedule, Gantt, Kanban, team load, tests and reports.

steps.title: Create or open a plan
steps.description:
A plan is a `plan/` folder of Markdown files in your workspace. Start from a template, or open a folder that already has `plan/project.md`. The user manual explains every feature with annotated screenshots.
[Create a project](command:planner.newProject)
[Open the user manual](command:planner.openManual)

steps.title: Add milestones, tasks and people
steps.description:
Use the + buttons in the Planner views (or the links above each line in a plan file) to add milestones, tasks, people and time off; right-click any task to edit it, change its status or owner, move or delete it. Everything is written as plain Markdown that you can also type yourself.
[Open the Planner sidebar](command:workbench.view.extension.planner)
[Add a task](command:planner.addTask)

steps.title: Schedule on the Gantt
steps.description:
Dates come from estimates, dependencies, capacity and time off. Drag a bar to set its start, resize it to change the estimate, link bars to add dependencies. Every change is a small, undoable edit of the Markdown.
[Open the Gantt](command:planner.openGantt)

media.altText: Gantt chart with milestones, task bars, dependencies and the critical path

steps.title: Work on the Kanban board
steps.description:
Move cards between columns to change status (start and done dates are written for you), with swimlanes per owner or milestone, WIP limits and a punch-list board.
[Open Kanban](command:planner.openKanban)

media.altText: Kanban board with To do, Doing, Review, Blocked and Done columns

steps.title: Balance the team load
steps.description:
Scheduled hours against capacity per person and ISO week, with time off. Switch to demand mode to see where work piles up.
[Open team load](command:planner.openResources)

media.altText: Heatmap of hours per person and week, coloured by load

steps.title: Track progress
steps.description:
Milestone forecasts against targets, burn-up, estimate accuracy, blocked and overdue work. Save a baseline to see slips later.
[Open the dashboard](command:planner.openDashboard)
[Save a baseline](command:planner.saveBaseline)

media.altText: Dashboard with KPIs, milestone cards and burn-up charts

steps.title: Run acceptance tests
steps.description:
Step through test cases, record pass, fail or n.a. with notes (keys P, F, N), raise punch items from failed steps and export the signed report.
[Open the test runner](command:planner.openTestRunner)

media.altText: Test runner with cases, steps and pass/fail buttons

steps.title: Share a status report
steps.description:
Export an HTML or PDF status report, Excel, MS Project XML or CSV into `plan/reports/`.
[Export…](command:planner.export)

steps.title: Optional: AI agents and MCP
steps.description:
Let Claude Code or Copilot agent mode build and run the plan: describe the project in plain text and the agent creates the team, milestones, tasks and dependencies through the planner's MCP server (New project sets it up). The skill tells agents how to work with the plan. The built-in AI commands propose changes as a diff that you accept or reject.
[Configure MCP for Claude Code](command:planner.configureMcp)
[Add the skill for AI agents](command:planner.addAgentSkill)
[Choose the AI provider](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22planner.ai%22%5D)

planner.planFolder.markdownDescription: Folder with the plan files, relative to the workspace folder (or absolute).

planner.me.markdownDescription: Your person id from `team.md`. Shown first in **My Work / Team**. Empty = the first person in `team.md`.

planner.autoAssignIds.markdownDescription: Add missing task ids (`^T…`) when a milestone file or the punch list is saved, and give a new id to a task line that was copied with its id and then given another title.

planner.autoAssignIdsOnAutoSave.markdownDescription: Also add missing ids when VS Code auto-saves after a delay (off, so ids do not appear while you type).

planner.autoSave.markdownDescription: Save the plan files after an edit made from a view (tree, Gantt, Kanban …). Edits stay undoable either way.

planner.editor.toggleOnClick.markdownDescription: Clicking inside a task's checkbox `[ ]` in the editor cycles its status (to do → in progress → review → done) and writes `@started`/`@done`. Off by default: a click meant to place the cursor changed the task. Hover the checkbox to change the status, or use **Planner: Cycle status** (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+X).

planner.editor.moveTasksAsBlocks.markdownDescription: **Alt+Up** / **Alt+Down** on a task line move the task with its notes and subtasks past the task above or below it at the same level. VS Code's own Move Line Up/Down moves only the line, which hands subtasks to another task. Other lines move as usual.

planner.confirmEarlyStart.markdownDescription: Ask before a task is started or finished while a milestone its milestone depends on (`depends:`) is not finished. Turn off if your milestones often overlap; the editor still points out work started early.

enumDescriptions: A to-do parent goes in progress when one of its subtasks starts, is done when its last subtask is done, and reopens when a subtask of a done parent reopens.
A parent's status only changes when you change it.
planner.parentStatus.markdownDescription: How a parent task's status follows its subtasks when a status is changed from the planner (commands, checkbox hover, Kanban, timer, task form, MCP). Finishing a task with open subtasks always asks whether to finish them too, cancel them or keep them open.

planner.codeLens.tasks.markdownDescription: Show the scheduled dates and slack above each task.

planner.codeLens.actions.markdownDescription: Show clickable actions next to the CodeLens: owner and **Edit** on tasks, **Add task**, **Add section** and **Edit milestone** on milestones, **Add person**, **Edit person**, **Add time off**, **Plan overtime** and **Add working day** in `team.md`, **Edit project settings** in `project.md`, **Capture to inbox** and **Plan into milestone…** in `inbox.md`, **Add punch item** in `punchlist.md`, **Open in test runner** in test plans. The schedule CodeLens stays.

planner.templatesFolder.markdownDescription: Folder with your own project templates (one sub-folder per template, Markdown files with `{{name}}`, `{{start}}`, `{{end}}`, `{{date:0.5}}` … placeholders). Relative to the first workspace folder or absolute.

planner.scheduling.unassignedCapacity.markdownDescription: Capacity in hours per week of the virtual **Unassigned** pool that runs tasks without `@owner`.

planner.diagnostics.overbooked.markdownDescription: Show an info diagnostic on a person in `team.md` when their workload makes tasks late: their open work, until when it is planned, and the tasks that finish after their deadline because of it.

planner.kanban.wipLimits.markdownDescription: Work-in-progress limit per Kanban column, e.g. `{ "doing": 4, "review": 3 }`. Columns over their limit are shown in red.

planner.time.roundingMinutes.markdownDescription: Timer time is rounded up to this many minutes before it is added to `@act` (at most 60). When the rounded time is more than a working day, stopping the timer asks first.

planner.todos.keywords.markdownDescription: Comment keywords collected in **TODOs in Code** (upper case, whole words, followed by `:`, `(…)` or a space).

planner.todos.include.markdownDescription: Glob of files searched for TODO comments (the plan folder is always skipped).

planner.todos.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob of files never searched for TODO comments.

planner.todos.maxFiles.markdownDescription: Maximum number of files searched for TODO comments.

planner.export.branding.markdownDescription: Branding of exported reports: `{ "company": "Example Corp", "accentColor": "#0f766e", "logo": "docs/logo.png" }` (logo relative to the workspace folder; PNG, JPEG, GIF, SVG or WebP, embedded in the report).

planner.export.periodDays.markdownDescription: Length of the reporting period in days ("done this period" and "planned next period").

planner.export.ganttWeeks.markdownDescription: Weeks shown in the report's Gantt and team load sections.

planner.export.author.markdownDescription: Author shown in reports. Empty = the name of `planner.me`.

planner.export.browserPath.markdownDescription: Path to Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome for PDF export. Empty = detect automatically; without a browser the HTML report is written instead.

planner.export.csvDelimiter.markdownDescription: Field delimiter of the CSV export (`;` suits Excel in many European locales).

planner.export.openAfterExport.markdownDescription: Open the exported file after `Planner: Export…`.

enumDescriptions: VS Code Language Model API: any installed model provider, e.g. GitHub Copilot.
Claude API directly; the key is stored with "Planner: Set API key".
No AI: AI commands are hidden; everything else works.
planner.ai.provider.markdownDescription: AI provider for the `Planner AI` commands. AI only proposes changes: every change is shown as a diff to accept or reject, and the scheduler (not the AI) computes all dates.

planner.ai.vscodeModel.markdownDescription: Model family for the `vscode-lm` provider (for example `gpt-4o` or `claude-sonnet-4`). Empty = the first available model.

planner.ai.model.markdownDescription: Claude model id for the `anthropic` provider.

planner.ai.redact.markdownDescription: Terms removed from prompts before they are sent (customer names …). Literal, case-insensitive terms, or `/regex/flags`.

planner.mcp.configureOnNewProject.markdownDescription: **New project** also writes `.mcp.json` with the md-planner MCP server and the agent skill (`.claude/skills/md-planner/SKILL.md`), so Claude Code and other agents can build and update the plan right away (same as **Planner: Configure MCP for Claude Code** and **Planner: Add the md-planner Skill for AI Agents**).
